name: 7,8-Dihydroxyflavone
papertitle: From cannabinoids and neurosteroids to statins and the ketogenic diet: New therapeutic avenues in Rett syndrome?
note: TrkB receptor agonist (BDNF receptor); reviewed as a neuroprotective candidate in RTT for its ability to mimic BDNF signaling without requiring the protein itself.
authors: Mouro, F. M., Miranda-Lourenço, C., Sebastião, A. M., & Diógenes, M. J. (2019)

name: Alanine
papertitle: Treating Rett syndrome: From mouse models to human therapies
note: Non-essential amino acid; reviewed within metabolic and nutritional strategies in RTT; role in the glucose-alanine cycle relevant to neuronal energy metabolism.
authors: Vashi, N., & Justice, M. J. (2019)

name: Allopregnanolone
papertitle: Time-dependent modulation of GABAA-ergic synaptic transmission by allopregnanolone in locus coeruleus neurons of Mecp2-null mice
note: Endogenous neurosteroid and positive modulator of GABA-A receptors; time-dependently modulated GABAergic transmission in locus coeruleus neurons of Mecp2-null mice.
authors: Jin, X., Zhong, W., & Jiang, C. (2013)

name: Benserazide
papertitle: Altered trajectories of neurodevelopment and behavior in mouse models of Rett syndrome
note: Peripheral dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor; combined with levodopa to increase central dopamine availability; evaluated in a RTT mouse model improving neurodevelopmental trajectories and behavior.
authors: Smith, E. S., Smith, D. R., Eyring, C., Braileanu, M., Smith-Connor, K. S., Ei Tan, Y., Fowler, A. Y., Hoffman, G. E., Johnston, M. V., Kannan, S., & Blue, M. E. (2019)

name: Blarcamesine
papertitle: The new big is small: Leveraging knowledge from small trials for rare disease drug development: Blarcamesine for Rett syndrome
note: Sigma-1 receptor agonist; evaluated in a clinical trial for RTT; a methodological study addressed how to leverage data from small trials for rare disease drug development.
authors: Ette, E. I., Fadiran, E. O., Missling, C., & Hammond, E. (2023)

name: Bromocriptine
papertitle: Bromocriptine in the Rett syndrome
note: D2 dopaminergic agonist; one of the earliest drugs evaluated in RTT; early clinical study explored its effect on the dopaminergic dysfunction observed in the syndrome.
authors: Zappella, M., Genazzani, A., Facchinetti, F., & Hayek, G. (1990)

name: Cannabidiol
papertitle: Cannabidiol therapy for refractory epilepsy and seizure disorders
note: Non-psychoactive cannabinoid with antiepileptic activity; reviewed for refractory epilepsy and seizure disorders; proposed as an alternative for RTT patients with treatment-resistant epilepsy.
authors: Golub, V., & Reddy, D. S. (2021)

name: Cannabivarin
papertitle: From cannabinoids and neurosteroids to statins and the ketogenic diet: New therapeutic avenues in Rett syndrome?
note: Phytocannabinoid analogue of cannabidiol with a shorter side chain; reviewed among cannabinoids and neurosteroids as possible therapeutic strategies in RTT.
authors: Mouro, F. M., Miranda-Lourenço, C., Sebastião, A. M., & Diógenes, M. J. (2019)

name: Carbamazepina
papertitle: Antiepileptic drugs in Rett syndrome
note: Sodium channel-blocking antiepileptic drug; documented in clinical use in RTT patients for seizure control; reviewed in a European multicenter study on antiepileptic drugs in RTT.
authors: Pintaudi, M., Calevo, M. G., Vignoli, A., Baglietto, M. G., Hayek, Y., Traverso, M., Giacomini, T., Giordano, L., Renieri, A., Russo, S., Canevini, M., & Veneselli, E. (2015)

name: Citalopram
papertitle: Fluoxetine rescues rotarod motor deficits in Mecp2 heterozygous mouse model of Rett syndrome via brain serotonin
note: SSRI reviewed in the context of serotonergic modulation in RTT; both citalopram and fluoxetine act on the serotonergic system which is disrupted in heterozygous Mecp2 mouse models.
authors: Villani, C., Sacchetti, G., Carli, M., & Invernizzi, R. W. (2020)

name: Clenbuterol
papertitle: Neurodevelopmental disorders: Righting Rett syndrome with IGF1
note: Beta-2 adrenergic agonist that stimulates IGF-1 production; proposed as a therapeutic strategy for RTT based on the IGF-1/PI3K signaling pathway.

name: Clonidina
papertitle: Management of self-injurious behaviors in children with neurodevelopmental disorders: A pharmacotherapy overview
note: Central alpha-2 adrenergic agonist; reviewed for management of self-injurious behaviors and hyperactivity in neurodevelopmental disorders including RTT.
authors: Sabus, A., Feinstein, J., Romani, P., Goldson, E., & Blackmer, A. (2019)

name: Curcumin
papertitle: Vascular dysfunction in a mouse model of Rett syndrome and effects of curcumin treatment
note: Natural polyphenol with anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties; corrected vascular dysfunction in a Mecp2-deficient RTT mouse model by improving vasodilatory responses.
authors: Panighini, A., Duranti, E., Santini, F., Maffei, M., Pizzorusso, T., Funel, N., Taddei, S., Bernardini, N., Ippolito, C., Virdis, A., & Costa, M. (2013)

name: CX546
papertitle: The enhancement of activity rescues the establishment of Mecp2 null neuronal phenotypes
note: Positive allosteric modulator of AMPA receptors (ampakine); rescued neuronal phenotypes in Mecp2-null cells by enhancing glutamatergic synaptic activity and neuronal plasticity.
authors: Scaramuzza, L., De Rocco, G., Desiato, G., Cobolli Gigli, C., Chiacchiaretta, M., Mirabella, F., Pozzi, D., De Simone, M., Conforti, P., Pagani, M., Benfenati, F., Cesca, F., Bedogni, F., & Landsberger, N. (2021)

name: Cysteamine
papertitle: Unexpected link between Huntington disease and Rett syndrome
note: Aminothiol with neuroprotective properties; identified through an unexpected link between Huntington disease and RTT; acts by elevating BDNF levels and reducing protein aggregate accumulation.
authors: Roux, J. C., Zala, D., Panayotis, N., Borges-Correia, A., Saudou, F., & Villard, L. (2012)

name: Desipramine
papertitle: Effect of desipramine on patients with breathing disorders in Rett syndrome
note: Tricyclic antidepressant (norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor); demonstrated improvement of breathing disorders in RTT patients in a clinical trial specifically targeting apneas and hyperpneas.
authors: Mancini, J., Dubus, J. C., Jouve, E., Roux, J. C., Franco, P., Lagrue, E., Castelnau, P., Cances, C., Chaix, Y., Rougeot-Jung, C., Cornu, C., Desportes, V., Vallée, L., Bahi-Buisson, N., Truillet, R., Attolini, L., Villard, L., Blin, O., & Micallef, J. (2017)

name: Dextromethorphan
papertitle: Randomized open-label trial of dextromethorphan in Rett syndrome
note: NMDA antagonist and sigma-1 agonist; evaluated in a randomized open-label clinical trial in RTT; showed trends of improvement in some behavioral symptoms without strong statistical significance.
authors: Smith-Hicks, C. L., Gupta, S., Ewen, J. B., Hong, M., Kratz, L., Kelley, R., Tierney, E., Vaurio, R., Bibat, G., Sanyal, A., Yenokyan, G., Brereton, N., Johnston, M. V., & Naidu, S. (2017)

name: Diazepam
papertitle: A case-controlled comparison of postoperative analgesic dosing between girls with Rett syndrome and girls with and without developmental disability undergoing spinal fusion surgery
note: GABA-A agonist benzodiazepine; studied in the context of postoperative pain management in girls with RTT undergoing spinal fusion surgery; useful for spasm and anxiety control.
authors: Barney, C. C., Merbler, A. M., Quest, K. et al. (2017)

name: Donepezil
papertitle: Mecp2 deletion from cholinergic neurons selectively impairs recognition memory and disrupts cholinergic modulation of the perirhinal cortex
note: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitor; Mecp2 deletion in cholinergic neurons selectively impaired recognition memory and cholinergic modulation; Donepezil proposed to correct this deficit.
authors: Ballinger, E. C., Schaaf, C. P., Patel, A. J., de Maio, A., Tao, H., Talmage, D. A., Zoghbi, H. Y., & Role, L. W. (2019)

name: Fingolimod
papertitle: Fingolimod in children with Rett syndrome: the FINGORETT study
note: Sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator evaluated in the FINGORETT clinical study in girls with Rett syndrome to reduce neuroinflammation and improve neurological function.
authors: Naegelin, Y., Kuhle, J., Schädelin, S. et al. (2021)

name: Fluoxetine
papertitle: Fluoxetine increases brain MeCP2 immuno-positive cells in a female Mecp2 heterozygous mouse model of Rett syndrome through endogenous serotonin
note: SSRI that increased MeCP2 immunopositive cells in heterozygous Mecp2 mice via endogenous serotonin; also rescued motor deficits in a heterozygous RTT mouse model.
authors: Villani, C., Carli, M., Castaldo, A. M., Sacchetti, G., & Invernizzi, R. W. (2021)

name: Folic acid
papertitle: Cerebral folate deficiency
note: Vitamin B9; reviewed in the context of cerebral folate deficiency that can coexist with RTT; involved in neurotransmitter synthesis and DNA methylation.
authors: Hyland, K., Shoffner, J., & Heales, S. J. (2010)

name: Gentamicin
papertitle: Evaluation of novel enhancer compounds in gentamicin-mediated readthrough of nonsense mutations in Rett syndrome
note: Aminoglycoside with nonsense mutation readthrough capacity; evaluated as an enhancer of functional MeCP2 protein production in MECP2 mutations that generate premature stop codons.
authors: Wong, K. M., Wegener, E., Baradaran-Heravi, A., Huppke, B., Gärtner, J., & Huppke, P. (2023)

name: Glutamic Acid
papertitle: RIPK1 activation in Mecp2-deficient microglia promotes inflammation and glutamate release in RTT
note: Excitatory neurotransmitter; RIPK1 activation in Mecp2-deficient microglia was shown to promote inflammation and excessive glutamate release in RTT pointing to the glutamatergic system as a therapeutic target.
authors: Cao, Z., Min, X., Xie, X., Huang, M., Liu, Y., Sun, W., Xu, G., He, M., He, K., Li, Y., & Yuan, J. (2024)

name: Lamotrigine
papertitle: Lamotrigine in two cases of Rett syndrome
note: Membrane-stabilizing antiepileptic drug; reported in two RTT clinical cases with seizure improvement; blocks sodium channels and modulates glutamate release.
authors: Kumandaş, S., Caksen, H., Ciftçi, A., Oztürk, M., & Per, H. (2001)

name: Levodopa
papertitle: Improvement of the Rett syndrome phenotype in a MeCP2 mouse model upon treatment with levodopa and a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor
note: Dopamine precursor used together with a dopa-decarboxylase inhibitor; improved phenotype in MeCP2-mutant mice with effects on motor function and the dopaminergic system.
authors: Szczesna, K., de la Caridad, O., Petazzi, P., Soler, M., Roa, L., Saez, M. A., Fourcade, S., Pujol, A., Artuch-Iriberri, R., Molero-Luis, M., Vidal, A., Huertas, D., & Esteller, M. (2014)

name: LM22A-4
papertitle: A small-molecule TrkB ligand improves dendritic spine phenotypes and atypical behaviors in female Rett syndrome mice
note: Small TrkB ligand (BDNF receptor); improved dendritic spine morphology and atypical behaviors in female RTT mice; promising preclinical results from a preprint study.
authors: Medeiros, D., Ayala-Baylon, K., Egido-Betancourt, H., Miller, E., Chapleau, C. A., Robinson, H. A., Phillips, M. L., Yang, T., Longo, F., Li, W., & Pozzo-Miller, L. (2023)

name: Lovastatin
papertitle: Lovastatin fails to improve motor performance and survival in methyl-CpG-binding protein2-null mice
note: HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor (statin); failed to improve motor performance and survival in Mecp2-null mice despite proposed neuroprotective mechanisms.
authors: Villani, C., Sacchetti, G., Bagnati, R., Passoni, A., Fusco, F., Carli, M., & Invernizzi, R. W. (2016)

name: Lysine
papertitle: Role of H3K4 demethylases in complex neurodevelopmental diseases
note: Essential amino acid with a role in post-translational histone modifications (H3K4 methylation); reviewed in the epigenetic context of complex neurodevelopmental diseases including RTT.
authors: Wynder, C., Stalker, L., & Doughty, M. L. (2010)

name: Melatonina
papertitle: Management of sleep disorders in children with neurodevelopmental disorders: A review
note: Neuroendocrine hormone with antioxidant properties; used in RTT for management of sleep disorders common in the syndrome; reviewed as part of pharmacological strategies in neurodevelopmental disorders.
authors: Blackmer, A. B., & Feinstein, J. A. (2016)

name: Memantine
papertitle: Is memantine a potential therapeutic for Rett syndrome?
note: Non-competitive NMDA receptor antagonist; proposed as therapy for RTT given the excitatory/inhibitory imbalance; systematic review of preclinical evidence.
authors: Bello, O., Blair, K., Chapleau, C., & Larimore, J. L. (2013)

name: Midazolam
papertitle: The benzodiazepine Midazolam mitigates the breathing defects of Mecp2-deficient mice
note: Short-acting benzodiazepine; mitigated breathing defects in Mecp2-deficient mice by acting on GABA-A receptors in respiratory brainstem centers.
authors: Voituron, N., & Hilaire, G. (2011)

name: Mirtazapine
papertitle: Mirtazapine treatment in a young female mouse model of Rett syndrome identifies time windows for the rescue of early phenotypes
note: Noradrenergic and serotonergic antidepressant; identified critical time windows for rescue of early phenotypes in a young RTT mouse model; effective before full symptom onset.
authors: Flores Gutiérrez, J., Natali, G., Giorgi, J., De Leonibus, E., & Tongiorgi, E. (2022)

name: Naltrexone
papertitle: Rett syndrome: Controlled study of an oral opiate antagonist, naltrexone
note: Opioid receptor antagonist; evaluated in a controlled trial in RTT; showed modest effects on breathing and behavior that were not sustained over time.
authors: Percy, A. K., Glaze, D. G., Schultz, R. J., Zoghbi, H. Y., Williamson, D., Frost, J. D. Jr., Jankovic, J. J., del Junco, D., Skender, M., & Waring, S. (1994)

name: Picrotin
papertitle: GABAA receptor antagonism ameliorates behavioral and synaptic impairments associated with MeCP2 overexpression
note: Inactive component of picrotoxin with a structure analogous to picrotoxinin; included as a structural reference; the study jointly evaluated GABA-A antagonism in the context of MeCP2 overexpression.
authors: Na, E. S., Morris, M. J., Nelson, E. D., & Monteggia, L. M. (2014)

name: Picrotoxinin
papertitle: GABAA receptor antagonism ameliorates behavioral and synaptic impairments associated with MeCP2 overexpression
note: Active component of picrotoxin; GABA-A receptor antagonist (chloride channel blocker); GABA-A antagonism ameliorated behavioral and synaptic impairments in mice overexpressing MeCP2.
authors: Na, E. S., Morris, M. J., Nelson, E. D., & Monteggia, L. M. (2014)

name: Risperidone
papertitle: Modulation of serotonin receptors in neurodevelopmental disorders: Focus on 5-HT7 receptor
note: Atypical antipsychotic D2 and 5-HT2 antagonist; reviewed for modulation of serotonin receptors (especially 5-HT7) in neurodevelopmental disorders such as RTT; used for behavioral symptom management.
authors: Lee, J., Avramets, D., Jeon, B., & Choo, H. (2021)

name: Sarizotan
papertitle: Potent hERG channel inhibition by sarizotan, an investigative treatment for Rett syndrome
note: 5-HT1A agonist and partial D2 agonist; investigated for RTT to manage apneas; identified as a potent hERG channel inhibitor representing an important cardiac safety signal.
authors: Cheng, H., Du, C., Zhang, Y., James, A. F., Dempsey, C. E., Abdala, A. P., & Hancox, J. C. (2019)

name: Tianeptina
papertitle: Drug repurposing in Rett and Rett-like syndromes: A promising yet underrated opportunity?
note: Atypical antidepressant modulating glutamate and serotonin; reviewed as a drug repurposing candidate for RTT and Rett-like syndromes.
authors: Fuchs, C., 't Hoen, P. A. C., Müller, A. R., Ehrhart, F., & Van Karnebeek, C. D. M. (2024)

name: Trazodona
papertitle: Drug repurposing in Rett and Rett-like syndromes: A promising yet underrated opportunity?
note: Serotonin reuptake inhibitor and 5-HT2 antagonist antidepressant; reviewed as a repurposing candidate for RTT in the context of mood and sleep symptoms.
authors: Fuchs, C., 't Hoen, P. A. C., Müller, A. R., Ehrhart, F., & Van Karnebeek, C. D. M. (2024)

name: Triheptanoin
papertitle: Anaplerotic triheptanoin diet enhances mitochondrial substrate use to remodel the metabolome and improve lifespan, motor function, and sociability in MeCP2-null mice
note: Anaplerotic 7-carbon medium-chain triglyceride; improved mitochondrial function and lifespan in Mecp2-null mice by remodeling the brain metabolome.
authors: Park, M. J., Aja, S., Li, Q., Degano, A. L., Penati, J., Zhuo, J., Roe, C. R., & Ronnett, G. V. (2014)

name: Trofinetide
papertitle: Trofinetide for the treatment of Rett syndrome: A randomized phase 3 study
note: Synthetic IGF-1 analogue; FDA-approved in 2023 (Daybue) for RTT in patients aged 2 and older; demonstrated improvement in behavioral symptoms and global function in a phase 3 clinical trial.
authors: Neul, J. L., Percy, A. K., Benke, T. A., Berry-Kravis, E. M., Glaze, D. G., Marsh, E. D., Lin, T., Stankovic, S., Bishop, K. M., & Youakim, J. M. (2023)

name: Trolox
papertitle: Systemic Radical Scavenger Treatment of a Mouse Model of Rett Syndrome: Merits and Limitations of the Vitamin E Derivative Trolox
note: Water-soluble vitamin E analogue with antioxidant activity; evaluated in RTT mice to reduce oxidative stress; showed partial benefits with long-term limitations.
authors: Janc, O. A., Hüser, M. A., Dietrich, K., Kempkes, B., Menzfeld, C., Hülsmann, S., & Müller, M. (2016)

name: Tyrosine
papertitle: Biochemical and clinical effects of tyrosine and tryptophan in the Rett syndrome
note: Catecholamine precursor amino acid; studied in RTT for its biochemical effects on dopamine and serotonin metabolism in combination with tryptophan.
authors: Nielsen, J. B., Lou, H. C., & Andresen, J. (1990)

name: Valproic acid
papertitle: SAMe, choline, and valproic acid as possible epigenetic drugs: Their effects in pregnancy with a special emphasis on animal studies
note: Antiepileptic drug with epigenetic properties (HDAC inhibitor); reviewed as an epigenetic agent with potential modulatory effect in RTT; also documented as a teratogen with a relevant risk profile.
authors: Ornoy, A., Weinstein-Fudim, L., & Becker, M. (2022)

name: Vatiquinone
papertitle: Profile of Trofinetide in the treatment of Rett syndrome: Design, development and potential place in therapy
note: Vitamin E analogue with mitochondrial antioxidant activity (15-LOX inhibitor); reviewed in the context of neuroprotection strategies in RTT alongside trofinetide.
authors: Camillo, L., Pozzi, M., Bernardo, P., Pisano, S., & Nobile, M. (2024)

name: Vigabatrin
papertitle: Epileptic spasms in CDKL5 deficiency disorder: Delayed treatment and poor response to first-line therapies
note: Irreversible GABA-transaminase inhibitor antiepileptic; documented in epileptic spasms in CDKL5 deficiency disorder (RTT-related); variable response to first-line therapies reported.
authors: Olson, H. E., Demarest, S., Pestana-Knight, E., Moosa, A. N., Zhang, X., Pérez-Pérez, J. R., Weisenberg, J., O'Connor Prange, E., Marsh, E. D., Rajaraman, R. R., Suter, B., Katyayan, A., Haviland, I., Daniels, C., Zhang, B., Greene, C., DeLeo, M., Swanson, L., Love-Nichols, J., Benke, T., Harini, C., & Poduri, A. (2023)
